ActiveTenants.description:
Active tenant counts from the messages and tenants tables.

active_24h is distinct tenants that sent or received a message in the
last 24 h; total_provisioned is non-deleted tenants in the tenants table.

active_24h.description: Tenants with message activity in last 24 h.
active_24h.title: Active 24H

ActiveTenants.title: ActiveTenants

AlertBand.description:
Variable-cost-vs-MRR row coloring on the cost dashboard.

Banded on per-tenant VARIABLE cost (Polaris COGS: Anthropic + Cohere +
OpenRouter) vs MRR — the true contribution margin. Fixed platform overhead
(Supabase/Redis/VPS/etc.) is tracked separately and is NOT in this ratio.
AlertBand.title: AlertBand

ApmErrors.description:
Sentry error count for the last 24 h (optional — requires sentry_auth_token).

configured=False when the token is not set; error_count_24h is NULL in
that case.  On a Sentry API error: configured=True, error_count_24h=NULL,
error contains the exception message.

error_count_24h.description: Sum of received errors over last 24 h from Sentry stats API.
error_count_24h.title: Error Count 24H

sentry_url.description: Sentry project browser URL when configured.
sentry_url.title: Sentry Url

ApmErrors.title: ApmErrors

Attachment.description:
One media item attached to an inbound message.

Phase 4's LLM consumer decides whether to download (Meta-hosted
media URLs have short TTLs and need a server-side fetch with the
Graph API token; IG and Messenger return permanent URLs in the
webhook itself; Chatwoot returns CDN URLs).
Attachment.title: Attachment

AuditChainVerification.description:
Read shape for ``GET /api/admin/audit/verifications/latest`` and
list endpoints.

Broken-row fields (broken_at_id / broken_at_created_at / broken_*_hash)
are NULL when status='intact'. When status='broken' they identify the
first row where the chain fails — start the investigation tree there
per ../docs/internal-ops/RUNBOOK.md "audit-chain break response".

broken_actual_hash_hex.description: Hex-encoded BYTEA of the row_hash found on the broken row (what the chain stored).
broken_actual_hash_hex.title: Broken Actual Hash Hex

broken_at_created_at.description: RFC3339 UTC of the broken row — useful for narrowing the investigation window.
broken_at_created_at.title: Broken At Created At

broken_at_id.description: audit_logs.id where the chain first broke. NULL when intact.
broken_at_id.title: Broken At Id

broken_prev_hash_hex.description: Hex-encoded BYTEA (lowercase, no 0x prefix) of the expected prev_hash (recomputed from the prior row). For transport-friendliness — the raw BYTEA is not JSON-safe.
broken_prev_hash_hex.title: Broken Prev Hash Hex

rows_scanned.description: Total audit_logs rows walked in this run.
rows_scanned.title: Rows Scanned

triggered_by_admin_id.description: Set when triggered_by='on_demand'. NULL for scheduled runs.
triggered_by_admin_id.title: Triggered By Admin Id

AuditChainVerification.title: AuditChainVerification

BroadcastDTO.description:
GET /api/tenant/broadcasts/{id} response shape.

Counters are read directly off the broadcasts row — they're
denormalised projections of broadcast_recipients.status counts,
maintained incrementally by the worker + the wa-status webhook.
BroadcastDTO.title: BroadcastDTO

BroadcastQueueDepth.description:
Broadcast worker queue snapshot from Phase 6.

Counters drawn from the broadcasts table (status enum
draft|scheduled|running|paused|completed|cancelled|errored) plus the
broadcast_recipients table (failed_last_hour).
BroadcastQueueDepth.title: BroadcastQueueDepth

BroadcastRecipientDTO.description:
GET /api/tenant/broadcasts/{id}/recipients row.

``skip_reason`` is a free-text column in the DB (see migration 043
header for the canonical values); we don't enum-restrict it here so
that a forward-compat operational marker (e.g. an admin manually
setting a recipient aside with a custom reason) doesn't fail
validation on the read path.
BroadcastRecipientDTO.title: BroadcastRecipientDTO

CSVImportErrorRow.description: One error from the importer's per-line error accumulator.
CSVImportErrorRow.title: CSVImportErrorRow

CSVImportResult.description:
Aggregate result of a CSV import attempt.

``imported_count`` covers both new inserts and updates to existing
active rows (re-import of an already-opted-in contact merges
locale + tags). ``skipped_count`` covers rows that were valid but
no-op'd (e.g. duplicate-in-file, or already-opted-out contacts the
importer chose not to re-activate). ``error_rows`` carries the
per-line accumulator — every row that didn't apply is here, with
the row_number from the source CSV preserved for tenant debugging.
CSVImportResult.title: CSVImportResult

ChunkingConfig.description:
Per-tenant chunk shape — read by the desktop at run time.

Returned from ``GET /api/admin/tenants/{tenant_id}/chunking-config``.
Service-role JWT only (tenants manage these values via the Phase 8
portal, NOT this endpoint). Defaults come from ADR-032 Amendment
(chunk_size=512, overlap=80); per-tenant overrides land in
``tenants.settings`` JSONB per Q-PHASE3-15.
ChunkingConfig.title: ChunkingConfig

CohereOverrideCost.description:
Row of the Cohere-Override subpanel.

Lists only tenants where ``tenants.cohere_rerank_enabled IS NOT NULL`` —
these are tenants with a per-tenant override of the Ultra+ tier gate
(ADR-026 Am.5). Operator alert fires when Cohere cost per overridden
tenant > 5% of their MRR (04 Phase 9 §9 spec).

alert.description: True when pct_of_mrr > 0.05 (i.e. Cohere alone > 5% MRR). Surfaces as an amber row in the subpanel; operator reviews monthly.
alert.title: Alert

CohereOverrideCost.title: CohereOverrideCost

ConversationDetail.description:
Detail-pane response: the conversation header + its messages
ordered oldest-first.

Per Q-PHASE8-08 + portal_design_prompt.md §2, the detail surface is
READ-ONLY. The "Reply in Chatwoot" CTA on the portal page is a
cross-domain link to ``chat.getpolaris.my`` — no write surface here.
ConversationDetail.title: ConversationDetail

ConversationListItem.description:
One row in the Conversations table.

``customer_display_name`` is pulled from ``conversations.metadata->>
'display_name'`` when present (the pipeline writes it from the
inbound webhook payload); when absent we fall back to a redacted
form of ``channel_user_id`` so the portal still renders a stable
identifier.

``last_intent`` reflects the most recent message's intent and helps
the operator spot conversations that ended in handoff or booking.

``message_count`` is a per-conversation aggregate; the index on
``messages(tenant_id, conversation_id, created_at)`` makes the
COUNT(*) acceptable at portal page sizes (≤ 50 rows per page).
ConversationListItem.title: ConversationListItem

ConversationListResponse.description:
Cursor-paginated list. Mirrors the notification feed shape so the
portal table primitive can be reused without divergence.

``next_cursor`` is opaque ``<rfc3339>|<uuid>`` — clients pass it back
verbatim. NULL when the page is the last one.
ConversationListResponse.title: ConversationListResponse

CreateBroadcastRequest.description:
POST /api/tenant/broadcasts body.

``scheduled_at=None`` => send immediately (the service layer sets
``scheduled_at = now()`` at materialisation time). Future scheduling
requires a UTC timestamp; the worker drains based on
``ZRANGEBYSCORE broadcast:queue:{tenant_id} -inf <now>``.
CreateBroadcastRequest.title: CreateBroadcastRequest

DashboardQuotaSummary.description:
Quota dials block.

Sourced from tenant_quotas (locked 16 columns per 05 §4.2) + period
counters maintained by Phase 4 (bot_replies), Phase 3 (knowledge),
Phase 6 (broadcasts), Phase 7 (bookings).
DashboardQuotaSummary.title: DashboardQuotaSummary

DashboardRecentConversation.description:
One row in the 5-row recent-conversations preview.

Sourced from conversations + last messages.intent_classified value.
Read-only viewer; replies live in Chatwoot (per portal_design_prompt.md §2).
DashboardRecentConversation.title: DashboardRecentConversation

DashboardSummary.description:
Full envelope for the Dashboard screen.

Single-round-trip per 04i §6.1: avoids a 6-call waterfall in the
initial paint. p95 budget ≤ 400 ms server-side.

active_broadcasts_count.description: Count of broadcasts in scheduled|sending status.
active_broadcasts_count.title: Active Broadcasts Count

active_promotions_count.description: Count of tenant_promotions where is_active=true and now() within valid_from..valid_until.
active_promotions_count.title: Active Promotions Count

ingestion_jobs_in_flight.description: Count of ingestion_requests in pending|running status.
ingestion_jobs_in_flight.title: Ingestion Jobs In Flight

plan_tier.description: Tenant's current plan tier (mirrors tenants.plan_tier). Drives the plan label on the Dashboard/Billing screens; without it the portal falls back to 'starter' and a Pro tenant is mislabelled.
plan_tier.title: Plan Tier

quota_replies_7d_sparkline.description: Last 7 days' daily bot_reply counts, oldest-first. Fixed length 7 so the portal sparkline component doesn't have to defend against ragged arrays.
quota_replies_7d_sparkline.title: Quota Replies 7D Sparkline

suspension_state.description: Mirrors tenants.suspended_reason. NULL = active. quota_exhausted → red banner, bot off, Chatwoot active (ADR-018). payment_overdue → route-takeover to /pay (ADR-049) — Dashboard rarely renders in this state since middleware redirects, but the field is here for completeness.
suspension_state.title: Suspension State

DashboardSummary.title: DashboardSummary

EmailDraftQueue.description:
Email assist draft queue snapshot from Phase 14.

Pending drafts are Chatwoot private notes awaiting agent action.
Accepted/edited/ignored counts are resolved_at outcomes over the last 24 h.

accepted_24h.description: Drafts accepted by agent in last 24 h.
accepted_24h.title: Accepted 24H

edited_24h.description: Drafts edited before send in last 24 h.
edited_24h.title: Edited 24H

latest_draft_at.description: RFC3339 UTC of most recent draft post.
latest_draft_at.title: Latest Draft At

EmailDraftQueue.title: EmailDraftQueue

FilterAllOptedIn.description:
Match every audience_members row where opted_out_at IS NULL.

The compiler always adds ``opted_out_at IS NULL`` to the outer
WHERE regardless of filter; this kind exists for tenants who want
"the whole list" without specifying any sub-criteria.
FilterAllOptedIn.title: FilterAllOptedIn

FilterBranch.description: Match a specific tenant_branch_id (Pro+ multi-branch tenants).
FilterBranch.title: FilterBranch

FilterChannel.description:
Match audience_members.channel ∈ given set.

Telegram is in the type union for v2.1 forward-compat but rejected
at the validation boundary today via the Literal restriction.
FilterChannel.title: FilterChannel

FilterCombinedAnd.description:
AND-combine 2..4 sub-filters; depth=1 only at GA.

Nesting a combined_and inside another combined_and is rejected by
the ``model_validator`` below. The SQL compiler would need a CTE
rewrite to support depth>=2 cleanly (parenthesised AND groups
nested under another AND group); deferred.
FilterCombinedAnd.title: FilterCombinedAnd

FilterTagsAll.description: Match if audience_members.tags is a superset of the given set (@>).
FilterTagsAll.title: FilterTagsAll

FilterTagsAny.description: Match if audience_members.tags overlaps the given set (&&).
FilterTagsAny.title: FilterTagsAny

HandoffInitiatedEventPayload.description:
Payload column of a webhook_events_outbound row when event_type='handoff.initiated'.

All UUIDs are tenant-scoped (audit trail). Timestamps are RFC3339 UTC
strings, not native datetimes, because asyncpg's JSONB serialiser
rejects datetime objects — the convention across all
webhook_events_outbound payloads is string-timestamps.

business_hours_state.description: Which handoff_message variant was sent to the customer (handoff_message_in_hours vs handoff_message_after_hours). ADR-019.
business_hours_state.title: Business Hours State

chatwoot_conversation_id.description: Chatwoot's conversation.id once the status flip succeeded. NULL on outcome != CONFIRMED (Chatwoot never accepted the flip).
chatwoot_conversation_id.title: Chatwoot Conversation Id

initiated_at.description: RFC3339 UTC. When Polaris's handoff service started the orchestration.
initiated_at.title: Initiated At

reason.description: Why the handoff fired. ``intent_classified`` = LLM detected handoff intent. ``stop_keyword`` = STOP / BERHENTI matcher fired (future v2.1 — currently STOP triggers opt-out, not handoff). ``flow_node`` = tenant-authored flow explicitly routes via a handoff node.
reason.title: Reason

requested_at.description: RFC3339 UTC. When the customer's handoff intent was classified — i.e. the timestamp of the inbound message that triggered handoff.
requested_at.title: Requested At

team_id.description: HandoffNode.team_id from the flow definition (Q-PHASE7-05: per-flow source only). String not int because flow definitions carry team_ids as strings (Chatwoot team_id is int — translated at the client layer).
team_id.title: Team Id

version.description: Payload version. Bumps when the schema breaks. v3.0 worker switches on this field to select the deserialiser.
version.title: Version

HandoffInitiatedEventPayload.title: HandoffInitiatedEventPayload

HandoffResult.description:
Returned by services/chatwoot/handoff.py::initiate_handoff.

Carried up through the flow runtime adapter into the handoff node
executor's NodeResult.decision payload, so flow authors can inspect
the outcome details via flow_run.step_trace.

reason.description: Set when outcome != 'confirmed'. Free-form classifier string (e.g. 'no_conversation', 'chatwoot_5xx_after_retries', 'team_not_found'). Carried into flow_run.step_trace for audit.
reason.title: Reason

HandoffResult.title: HandoffResult

HealthSnapshot.description:
Aggregate read for ``GET /api/admin/health``.

Signals are loaded in parallel server-side; an outage on any one
renders that tile only (no fail-the-whole-page) per the
silent-failure-hunter gate in PR-6.
HealthSnapshot.title: HealthSnapshot

HealthStatus.description: Single source of truth for the GET /health response shape.
HealthStatus.title: HealthStatus

IncomingMessage.description:
Normalised inbound event emitted by the webhook dispatcher.

Consumer contract:
  - The same shape is enqueued whether the source is Meta (WA / IG /
    Messenger) or Chatwoot. Per-channel quirks live in the
    dispatcher, NOT here.
  - ``received_at`` is the Polaris-server receive time; use that for
    Polaris-side ordering. ``provider_sent_at`` is the
    provider-claimed send time when present and is useful for
    latency measurements + log correlation, but should not gate
    application logic (provider clocks drift).
  - ``body`` may be ``None`` for media-only messages; consumers
    must handle the ``attachments`` list independently. For WA
    media-with-caption messages the caption lands in ``body``
    (caption is conversational intent; treating it specially would
    force every consumer to merge two text sources).
  - ``in_reply_to`` is the provider-side id of the message being
    replied to when the user used a reply / quote feature.
    ``None`` for the common case (new message, not a reply).
IncomingMessage.title: IncomingMessage

IngestionRequestResponse.description:
Tenant-facing response for POST/GET on ``/api/tenant/knowledge/requests``.

``eta`` = ``submitted_at + 24h`` per PRD §6.2 SLA. ``status_url`` is
a relative path the portal can poll without hard-coding the API host.
Counts (``chunks_added`` / ``_skipped`` / ``_deleted``) are NULL
until the desktop processes the row.
IngestionRequestResponse.title: IngestionRequestResponse

IngestionRequestSubmit.description:
Tenant-facing request body for ``POST /api/tenant/knowledge/requests``.

Pydantic-side shape validation parallels the SQL CHECK so callers
see a clean 422 instead of a 500 + integrity-error round-trip.
Field bounds match the desktop's safe operating envelope (crawl
depth ≤ 10, pages ≤ 2000, OCR languages ≤ 4) so a runaway request
can't burn an arbitrary amount of desktop CPU before its own caps
kick in.
IngestionRequestSubmit.title: IngestionRequestSubmit

IssueInvoiceRequest.description:
Request body for ``POST /api/admin/billing/invoices``.

The router computes invoice_number via the invoice_sequence table,
populates issued_at + status='open', and renders + uploads the PDF.
period is a free-text label per migration 008 (e.g. '2026-06' for
monthly, '2026' for annual); proration_basis JSONB carries the
richer breakdown (kind, period_start/end, subtotal/tax split,
quote reference, renderer_version) for audit.

amount_myr.description: Final charge to the tenant. Tax breakdown lives in proration_basis JSONB.
amount_myr.title: Amount Myr

due_at.description: RFC3339 UTC. Daily cron flips status -> overdue when NOW() > due_at AND status = 'open'.
due_at.title: Due At

proration_basis.description: JSONB snapshot per 00c §12.4.1. Convention keys: {kind, period_start, period_end, subtotal_myr, tax_myr, original_tier, target_tier, prorate_basis, quote_id, renderer_version}. Audit-grade; do not mutate after issue.
proration_basis.title: Proration Basis

IssueInvoiceRequest.title: IssueInvoiceRequest

KnowledgeChunkHit.description:
One row from ``match_knowledge_chunks`` / ``_hybrid``.

Per-field semantics:
  * ``id`` — knowledge_chunks.id (UUID).
  * ``content`` — full chunk text (bounded by chunker; ADR-032
    default 512 tokens, per-tenant override via tenants.settings).
  * ``source_name`` — display label (URL, filename, etc.) for
    citation rendering in Phase 8 portal.
  * ``rrf_score`` — primary sort key, higher = better. Always
    populated.
  * ``vector_rank`` / ``bm25_rank`` — 1-based ranks within the
    candidate pool for each leg; ``None`` when the chunk only
    matched the OTHER leg (FULL OUTER JOIN in the hybrid RPC).
  * ``distance`` — populated by the vector-only fallback; ``None``
    from the hybrid RPC.
KnowledgeChunkHit.title: KnowledgeChunkHit

KnowledgeGapCaptures.description:
Knowledge gap miss captures from Phase 15 (Ultra-tier only).

Counts are drawn from knowledge_gap_misses over the last 24 h, grouped
by signal_type (no_retrieval | low_retrieval | handoff).

latest_at.description: RFC3339 UTC of most recent gap capture.
latest_at.title: Latest At

total_24h.description: Sum of all signal types over last 24 h.
total_24h.title: Total 24H

KnowledgeGapCaptures.title: KnowledgeGapCaptures

KnowledgeGapExample.description:
One raw miss row for a theme's drill-down view.

Returned by ``GET /api/tenant/knowledge-gaps/summary/examples``.
``conversation_id`` links to the portal conversation detail page.

conversation_id.description: UUID of the conversation this miss belongs to.
conversation_id.title: Conversation Id

created_at.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp of when the miss was captured.
created_at.title: Created At

customer_question.description: Raw inbound question text that went unanswered.
customer_question.title: Customer Question

KnowledgeGapExample.title: KnowledgeGapExample

KnowledgeGapExamplesResponse.description: Envelope for the drill-down examples endpoint.

examples.description: Raw miss rows for the requested theme, newest-first, capped at 20.
examples.title: Examples

KnowledgeGapExamplesResponse.title: KnowledgeGapExamplesResponse

KnowledgeGapTheme.description:
One clustered gap — a group of near-identical unanswered questions.

v1 grouping is by normalized question text (lowercase, punctuation-stripped,
whitespace-collapsed), so distinct phrasings may not merge until the M2
semantic-clustering upgrade. ``example_question`` is the most-recent raw
phrasing in the group, shown to the tenant verbatim.

``norm_q`` is the stable grouping key — pass it as the ``q`` param to
``GET /summary/examples`` to fetch the contributing raw rows.

ask_count.description: Total misses in this theme within the window.
ask_count.title: Ask Count

example_question.description: Most-recent raw phrasing in this group (display verbatim).
example_question.title: Example Question

last_seen.description: RFC3339 UTC of the most recent miss.
last_seen.title: Last Seen

low_retrieval_count.description: Misses signalled by low RAG retrieval score.
low_retrieval_count.title: Low Retrieval Count

no_retrieval_count.description: Misses signalled by zero RAG retrieval.
no_retrieval_count.title: No Retrieval Count

norm_q.description: Stable normalized key for this theme group (lowercase, punctuation→space, whitespace-collapsed). Pass as `q` to GET /summary/examples for drill-down.
norm_q.title: Norm Q

recent_count.description: Misses in the last 7 days — a trend hint (rising if a large share of ask_count).
recent_count.title: Recent Count

KnowledgeGapTheme.title: KnowledgeGapTheme

KnowledgeGapsSummary.description: Full envelope for the Knowledge Gaps screen — one round-trip.

themes.description: Ranked gap themes, highest ask_count first (capped server-side).
themes.title: Themes

total_misses.description: Total miss rows in the window (pre-grouping).
total_misses.title: Total Misses

window_days.description: Look-back window the themes were aggregated over.
window_days.title: Window Days

KnowledgeGapsSummary.title: KnowledgeGapsSummary

KnowledgeSourceCreate.description:
Tenant-facing request body for ``POST /api/tenant/knowledge/sources``.

Pydantic-side shape validation parallels the SQL CHECK in migration 118
so callers see a clean 422 instead of a 500 + integrity-error round-trip.

``desired_hash`` is caller-supplied:
  * url  → SHA-256(url string)  — stable as long as the URL is unchanged
  * file → SHA-256(file bytes)  — computed browser-side before the sign step
  * text → SHA-256(source_text) — computed from the body text

The reconciler uses this to skip unchanged sources on every Sync run.
KnowledgeSourceCreate.title: KnowledgeSourceCreate

KnowledgeSourceResponse.description:
Tenant-facing response for POST/GET on ``/api/tenant/knowledge/sources``.

Intentionally lean: ``desired_hash`` and ``source_text`` body are
omitted — they are reconciler-internal and potentially large.
``source_url`` and ``storage_path`` are included so the portal can
display the source location. ``status`` + ``chunk_count`` +
``last_synced_at`` power the reconciliation state column.
KnowledgeSourceResponse.title: KnowledgeSourceResponse

LlmTokenBurn.description:
LLM token throughput from the ``messages`` table.

Authoritative MYR spend lives in Grafana Cloud (the Cost dashboard);
``est_cost_myr_mtd`` here is a local best-effort estimate from token
counts and is NULL when no pricing map is available.

est_cost_myr_mtd.description: Local estimate; Cost dashboard (Mimir) is source of record.
est_cost_myr_mtd.title: Est Cost Myr Mtd

LlmTokenBurn.title: LlmTokenBurn

MessageDetail.description:
One message in the read-only detail pane.

The shape carries the bot-side telemetry the operator wants to see —
intent, which model the dispatcher picked, response latency, how
many RAG chunks fed the reply — but **not** the chunk contents
themselves (RAG bodies live in ``knowledge_chunks`` and surfacing
them would bloat the payload for no portal-side use case).

Tokens are optional everywhere because pre-Phase-4 messages don't
carry telemetry and inbound user messages are never tokenized at
write time (the loader heuristic kicks in only when a window is
being assembled for the LLM).
MessageDetail.title: MessageDetail

MessagingVolume.description:
Conversation throughput from the ``messages`` table.

Direction inferred from ``role`` (user = inbound, assistant = outbound).
bot_replies_mtd comes from ``tenant_usage`` (metered bot replies this
billing month, summed across tenants).
MessagingVolume.title: MessagingVolume

MessengerGetStarted.description:
The 'Get Started' button shown on the welcome screen.

Customers who have never messaged the Page see a single CTA button
on the empty conversation. Tapping fires this payload to the bot,
which typically routes to the onboarding flow.

payload.description: Postback payload fired when customer taps the 'Get Started' button. Polaris convention: 'get_started' (literal string) or 'get_started:<flow_slug>'.
payload.title: Payload

MessengerGetStarted.title: MessengerGetStarted

MessengerIcebreaker.description:
One icebreaker entry in the messenger_profile.ice_breakers array.

Shown as a tappable chip above the message-input box when a customer
first opens the FB Messenger conversation with the tenant's Page.
Tapping sends ``payload`` to the bot as a postback (not as the
visible question text).

payload.description: Bot-side postback payload when customer taps the icebreaker. Polaris convention: prefix with 'icebreaker:' for routing (e.g. 'icebreaker:hours'). Meta cap: 1000 chars.
payload.title: Payload

MessengerIcebreaker.title: MessengerIcebreaker

MessengerPersistentMenu.description:
One locale-scoped persistent menu.

``locale='default'`` applies cross-locale (Meta's wildcard).
Specific locales (e.g. ``locale='zh_CN'``) override the default for
customers whose Messenger UI is in that locale.

``composer_input_disabled=True`` removes the free-text input box —
customers can ONLY interact via the menu CTAs and icebreakers. Used
by tenants with strictly menu-driven flows (booking-only, FAQ-only).

call_to_actions.description: 1-3 CTAs per Meta. Order = display order top-to-bottom in the menu.
call_to_actions.title: Call To Actions

composer_input_disabled.description: If True, customer cannot type free text — menu-only interaction.
composer_input_disabled.title: Composer Input Disabled

MessengerPersistentMenu.title: MessengerPersistentMenu

MessengerProfileBundle.description:
Full bundle PUT to Meta /messenger_profile.

Q-PHASE7-06: Phase 7 always PUTs all three sections, even when the
tenant only edited one. Simpler code, fewer Meta edge cases (partial
PUT semantics are inconsistent across Meta SDK versions).

Empty lists (``ice_breakers=[]``, ``persistent_menu=[]``) clear those
sections in Meta. ``get_started=None`` is the only way to UNSET that
section — a None means "feature not configured".

get_started.description: Welcome-screen CTA. None means feature not configured / cleared.

ice_breakers.description: Up to 4 icebreakers per Meta. Empty list clears the section.
ice_breakers.title: Ice Breakers

persistent_menu.description: Per-locale menus. Empty list clears the section.
persistent_menu.title: Persistent Menu

MessengerProfileBundle.title: MessengerProfileBundle

MessengerProfilePushResult.description:
Returned by services/messenger_profile.py::push_profile.

``diff_against_remote`` carries the partial-success surface: Meta
sometimes returns 200 even when a subset of fields didn't update
(e.g. an icebreaker with an emoji that violates a locale rule
survives validation but is silently dropped). We re-GET after every
push and surface the diff in this field for the portal to render.

diff_against_remote.description: Non-None when re-GET of /messenger_profile shows mismatch vs what we sent. Keys map to bundle sections; values describe the drift. Drives portal 'out-of-sync' banner.
diff_against_remote.title: Diff Against Remote

error.description: Classified error string when success=False. Vocabulary: 'meta_400_invalid_payload', 'meta_401_token_revoked', 'meta_5xx_after_retries', 'timeout'.
error.title: Error

pushed_at.description: RFC3339 UTC instant of POST completion.
pushed_at.title: Pushed At

MessengerProfilePushResult.title: MessengerProfilePushResult

MetaRateLimitHeadroom.description:
Meta Graph API rate-limit headroom per surface.

Polaris captures the ``X-Business-Use-Case-Usage`` header from
every Meta call and averages it over the last 24 h. calls_remaining_pct
is 100 - usage (so 100% = full headroom, 0% = throttled).
MetaRateLimitHeadroom.title: MetaRateLimitHeadroom

Notification.description:
One row in the portal feed. Shape returned by
``GET /api/tenant/notifications`` and ``PATCH .../{id}``.

Timestamps are RFC3339 UTC strings (asyncpg's JSONB serialiser
rejects datetime objects, and the column reads come back as
``datetime`` which we ``.isoformat()`` at the router layer — the
string contract here is what the portal sees).

href.description: Click-through path to the relevant portal screen.
href.title: Href

metadata.description: Free-form renderer-side payload (template_id, broadcast_id, invoice_number, etc.). Schema is per-kind; not validated at the Notification level so adding a kind doesn't require a shape bump.
metadata.title: Metadata

recipient_user_id.description: NULL = tenant-wide; non-NULL = single auth.users row.
recipient_user_id.title: Recipient User Id

Notification.title: Notification

NotificationKind.description:
Catalogued event kinds. Match the comment block on
``notifications.kind`` in migration 051.

Strings (not opaque ints) so the bell-icon UI can switch on the
value directly without an extra lookup. Past-tense aligned with
ADR-051's outbound-webhook naming convention.
NotificationKind.title: NotificationKind

NotificationListResponse.description:
Envelope for ``GET /api/tenant/notifications``.

Cursor pagination: ``next_cursor`` is opaque (currently the
created_at of the last item, but the contract makes no promise so
we can switch to a tie-breaker key without changing the wire shape).

next_cursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page. NULL on the last page. Pass back as ?cursor=… on the follow-up request.
next_cursor.title: Next Cursor

unread_count.description: Total unread across all kinds for this tenant. Drives the bell-icon badge; computed cheaply via the partial index on notifications(tenant_id, created_at DESC) WHERE read_at IS NULL.
unread_count.title: Unread Count

NotificationListResponse.title: NotificationListResponse

marked_count.description: How many notifications transitioned unread → read.
marked_count.title: Marked Count

NotificationMarkReadRequest.description:
Body for ``PATCH /api/tenant/notifications/{id}``.

Idempotent: setting read=true twice is a no-op. Setting read=false
on an already-read notification clears the marker (rare; supports
the "mark unread" UI affordance).
NotificationMarkReadRequest.title: NotificationMarkReadRequest

OptOutViewerPage.description:
Paginated opt-out viewer response.

Cursor-based pagination (opaque base64) so a large tenant's opt-out
list paginates stably even as new rows arrive. ``total_count`` is
a SELECT COUNT(*) under the same RLS-scoped WHERE — cheap because
the audience_members.opted_out_at partial index makes it an
index-only scan.
OptOutViewerPage.title: OptOutViewerPage

OptOutViewerRow.description:
One row in the opt-out viewer.

Carries the three PDPA-required columns (opted_out_at,
opted_out_reason, opted_out_at_channel) plus enough identifying
info that a human agent can confirm "yes this is the right person
to NOT re-engage". phone_number_e164 is intentionally kept — under
PDPA, an opt-out list that hides the contact identifier is useless
for downstream agents checking before manual outreach.
OptOutViewerRow.title: OptOutViewerRow

PerIntentTierBreakdown.description:
One row of the per-intent-tier table on the per-tenant cost page.

intent_tier mirrors ``polaris_shared_types.llm_response.IntentTier``
values (simple | medium | hard); the 'handoff' Literal value is
excluded because handoffs bypass the LLM entirely. Kept as plain
string here (not the Literal) because the dashboard surface is
label-driven and we may add tiers post-GA.

avg_cache_read_tokens.description: Non-zero indicates prompt cache is hitting; supports the Phase 4 exit-criterion-1 verification.
avg_cache_read_tokens.title: Avg Cache Read Tokens

cache_hit_rate.description: cache_read_tokens / (cache_read_tokens + input_tokens) over the sample. Surfaces in the cost-cutting revisit banner if < 30% after 4 weeks (signals system prompt churning or TTL too short).
cache_hit_rate.title: Cache Hit Rate

model_used.description: Resolved model per ADR-031 routing — e.g. 'haiku' or 'sonnet'. Mirrors ``messages.model_used`` values.
model_used.title: Model Used

sample_count.description: Number of LLM calls in the window.
sample_count.title: Sample Count

PerIntentTierBreakdown.title: PerIntentTierBreakdown

PersistentMenuCallToAction.description:
One entry inside a persistent_menu.call_to_actions array.

Two flavours: ``postback`` (carries a payload back to the bot) and
``web_url`` (opens a URL in the Messenger in-app browser).

payload.description: Required when type='postback'. Bot postback payload. Meta cap: 1000 chars.
payload.title: Payload

url.description: Required when type='web_url'. https-only per Meta policy. Meta cap: 2048 chars.
url.title: Url

PersistentMenuCallToAction.title: PersistentMenuCallToAction

PlanChangeApprovalRequest.description:
Request body for ``POST /api/admin/plan-changes/{id}/approve``.

The admin frontend supplies an optional decision_note (free-form
text shown to the tenant) and an optional override of the
server-recomputed proration. If proration_override is omitted, the
server's authoritative recomputation is used. If supplied, the
override is what lands on the issued invoice — must be used
sparingly and with reason in decision_note.

decision_note.description: Optional free-form note surfaced to the tenant in the approval notification + portal Billing screen.
decision_note.title: Decision Note

proration_override.description: Optional override of the server-recomputed proration (per 00c §12.4.1). If supplied, decision_note MUST explain why — typical use is a sales-led one-off adjustment.
proration_override.title: Proration Override

PlanChangeApprovalRequest.title: PlanChangeApprovalRequest

PlanChangeRejectionRequest.description:
Request body for ``POST /api/admin/plan-changes/{id}/reject``.

decision_note is required on rejection — the tenant sees the reason
in their portal Billing screen.

decision_note.description: Required. Tenant sees this in their portal Billing screen + the plan_change_rejected notification.
decision_note.title: Decision Note

PlanChangeRejectionRequest.title: PlanChangeRejectionRequest

PlanChangeRequest.description:
Read shape for ``GET /api/tenant/plan-change-requests/{id}`` and
response body of ``POST /api/tenant/plan-change-requests``.

All timestamps RFC3339 UTC strings (asyncpg datetimes are isoformatted
at the router layer).

decided_by_user_id.description: Phase 10 admin auth.users.id; NULL while pending.
decided_by_user_id.title: Decided By User Id

PlanChangeRequest.title: PlanChangeRequest

PlanChangeRequestCreate.description:
Request body for ``POST /api/tenant/plan-change-requests``.

Tenant supplies only target tier + cycle + optional reason. Server
fills current_tier/current_billing_cycle from tenant_quotas + computes
proration_preview at insert time.

reason.description: Optional tenant message; surfaces in admin approval UI.
reason.title: Reason

PlanChangeRequestCreate.title: PlanChangeRequestCreate

PlatformAdmin.description:
Read shape returned by the admin API to the admin frontend.

The frontend never receives more than this — there are no tokens or
secrets on a platform_admin row. NextAuth holds the session JWT
independently.

active.description: Soft-deactivate (FALSE) on departure so audit FKs survive. INSERT sets TRUE; UPDATE flips to FALSE.
active.title: Active

last_login_at.description: RFC3339 UTC; NULL before first login.
last_login_at.title: Last Login At

last_login_ip.description: IP captured on last successful magic-link consumption — used as the bound IP for the IP-bind callback per ADR-030 Am.2026-05-20.
last_login_ip.title: Last Login Ip

PlatformAdmin.title: PlatformAdmin

PlatformCostSummary.description:
Platform P&L for a month — fixed vs variable kept separate (no amortization).

gross_margin = Σ MRR − (Σ per-tenant variable cost + Σ active fixed costs).

fixed_costs.description: Active fixed-cost line items behind total_fixed_cost_myr.
fixed_costs.title: Fixed Costs

gross_margin_myr.description: total_mrr − total_variable − total_fixed. May be negative.
gross_margin_myr.title: Gross Margin Myr

PlatformCostSummary.title: PlatformCostSummary

PlatformFixedCost.description:
One operator-entered fixed/global platform cost line item.

Fixed costs are NOT measured per tenant (Supabase plan, Redis, VPS,
Grafana, Sentry, domains, …). The operator maintains these line items in
the admin Cost page; the monthly total feeds the platform P&L. Persisted
in the ``platform_fixed_costs`` table (migration 086).

active.description: Inactive line items are excluded from totals.
active.title: Active

PlatformFixedCost.title: PlatformFixedCost

ProductHit.description:
One row from ``match_products`` / ``match_products_hybrid``.

Per-field semantics mirror ``KnowledgeChunkHit``:
  * ``rrf_score`` — primary sort key, higher = better. Always populated.
  * ``vector_rank`` / ``bm25_rank`` — 1-based ranks within each leg's
    candidate pool; ``None`` when the product only matched the other
    leg (FULL OUTER JOIN in the hybrid RPC).
  * ``distance`` — populated by the vector-only fallback; ``None`` from
    the hybrid RPC.
ProductHit.title: ProductHit

ProrationPreview.description:
Snapshot computed at request time per 00c §12.4.1.

Phase 10 admin recomputes authoritative on approval; the request-time
snapshot is a tenant-transparency artifact, not the source of truth.
If admin's recomputed amount diverges from this snapshot (e.g. tier
pricing changed between request + approval), admin path surfaces the
delta in ``decision_note`` so the tenant sees why.

amount_due_myr.description: Net charge for the change. 0 = tier downgrade with prorated credit consumed by next invoice.
amount_due_myr.title: Amount Due Myr

period_credited_myr.description: Unused current-period amount credited towards the new tier. 0 if request fires at period boundary.
period_credited_myr.title: Period Credited Myr

prorate_basis.description: How the proration was computed. GA uses calendar_month (invoice fires on the 1st per 00c §12.4.1). 'anniversary' is the v2.1+ option for tenants on a custom billing date.
prorate_basis.title: Prorate Basis

quota_topup_bot_replies.description: Additional bot_replies headroom granted immediately on approval (tier-up only; tier-down is 0).
quota_topup_bot_replies.title: Quota Topup Bot Replies

ProrationPreview.title: ProrationPreview

QuotaSaturation.description: Bot-reply quota saturation across tenants (tenant_usage vs tenant_quotas).
QuotaSaturation.title: QuotaSaturation

QuotaSaturationTenant.description: A single tenant's bot-reply quota saturation this period.
QuotaSaturationTenant.title: QuotaSaturationTenant

QuoteGenerateRequest.description:
Request body for ``POST /api/admin/quotes``.

All other fields (quote_code, proration_inputs, pdf coordinates,
expires_at) are server-computed.

intended_signup_date.description: ISO date YYYY-MM-DD. The prorated first invoice + quota are computed for the partial period from this date through the end of the calendar month (or anniversary cycle if requested via proration_basis).
intended_signup_date.title: Intended Signup Date

QuoteGenerateRequest.title: QuoteGenerateRequest

QuotePdfMeta.description:
Inline summary shown on the admin frontend before PDF render.

Lets the operator confirm the numbers BEFORE the bytes are persisted
to Supabase Storage. After PDF render this metadata is also serialised
into ``sales_quotes.proration_inputs`` for byte-stability across
re-downloads.

expires_at.description: RFC3339 UTC; default 30 days from generation.
expires_at.title: Expires At

first_invoice_myr.description: Prorated charge for the partial first period.
first_invoice_myr.title: First Invoice Myr

first_period_reply_cap.description: Prorated bot_replies cap for the partial first period.
first_period_reply_cap.title: First Period Reply Cap

headline_price_myr.description: Full-period subscription price for target tier.
headline_price_myr.title: Headline Price Myr

headline_reply_cap.description: Full-period bot_replies cap for target tier.
headline_reply_cap.title: Headline Reply Cap

QuotePdfMeta.title: QuotePdfMeta

RecentFailures.description: Recent failure counters + deep-links to the full APM tooling.
RecentFailures.title: RecentFailures

RedisStatus.description:
Redis connectivity probe.

``INFO`` aggregation; used_memory_mb shown alongside healthy/error.

used_memory_mb.description: Reported by INFO; NULL when last probe failed.
used_memory_mb.title: Used Memory Mb

RedisStatus.title: RedisStatus

SalesQuote.description:
Read shape for ``GET /api/admin/quotes`` (and the per-id endpoint).

The PDF download is a separate signed-URL redirect through
``GET /api/admin/quotes/{id}/pdf``; this shape carries the bucket
coordinates only.

converted_to_tenant_id.description: Set on conversion via ``POST /api/admin/quotes/{id}/convert/{tenant_id}``. NULL while the quote remains unconverted.
converted_to_tenant_id.title: Converted To Tenant Id

proration_inputs.description: Inputs for re-render: prorate_basis, days_remaining_in_period, headline_price, prorated_invoice, prorated_quota, renderer_version. Combined with the bucketed PDF bytes this gives byte-stable re-downloads per Q-PHASE9-05.
proration_inputs.title: Proration Inputs

SalesQuote.title: SalesQuote

SenderRef.description:
Channel-native sender identity.

NOT a Polaris ``tenant_users.user_id`` — that's the operator side.
``channel_user_id`` is whatever the provider hands us:
  - WA:        E.164 phone number ('60123456789')
  - IG / FB:   the platform's user / page-scoped id
  - Chatwoot:  the contact id (stringified)
  - Telegram:  the chat id (stringified numeric; stable per user<->bot)

``display_name`` is best-effort and may be ``None`` on first contact
(WA doesn't include profile name until the recipient has saved the
business in their contacts).
SenderRef.title: SenderRef

ServiceConnectivity.description:
HTTP reachability probe for an external service (Chatwoot or EA fork).

healthy=True when the service returns any HTTP response (even 4xx/401);
healthy=False on connection error or timeout. latency_ms is NULL when
the probe failed. Reused for both the chatwoot and ea tiles.
ServiceConnectivity.title: ServiceConnectivity

SupabaseStatus.description:
Supabase connectivity probe.

A simple ``SELECT 1`` against the polaris_service pool plus the
timing. ``healthy=False`` + error string when the probe fails;
db_latency_ms NULL in that case.

db_latency_ms.description: 60-second rolling average; NULL when last probe failed.
db_latency_ms.title: Db Latency Ms

SupabaseStatus.title: SupabaseStatus

TemplateButton.description:
One button inside a BUTTONS component.

Quick-reply buttons carry only ``text``. URL + phone-number buttons
carry ``url`` / ``phone_number`` respectively. Meta enforces that
each component holds at most 3 buttons; we don't repeat that here
because the BUTTONS-component validator below applies the cap.
TemplateButton.title: TemplateButton

TemplateComponent.description:
One component of a Meta message template.

Meta's wire shape is loosely typed (``components[]`` mixes HEADER
with TEXT format, BODY with text, FOOTER with text, BUTTONS with
nested buttons). We keep it loose here too — a tighter discriminated
union on ``type`` would be cleaner but the cost is heavy when most
templates only carry a BODY component anyway.
TemplateComponent.title: TemplateComponent

TenantBranch.description:
Row shape for `tenant_branches`.

Beyond ``name``, the operational columns are surfaced so the portal can edit
them: per-branch ``business_hours`` (same shape as ``tenants.business_hours``,
NULL = inherit tenant default), handoff-message overrides (ADR-019), and the
EA provider/service routing (migration 080). ``slug`` is read-only.
TenantBranch.title: TenantBranch

TenantBranchUpsert.description:
Body shape for create + update.

``name`` is required. The operational fields are optional; on UPDATE a
null/omitted field leaves the stored value unchanged (COALESCE semantics),
so editing hours never clears the provisioning-written ``ea_*`` ids. ``slug``
is read-only (auto-managed at provisioning) and not settable here.
TenantBranchUpsert.title: TenantBranchUpsert

TenantCostMonthly.description:
One row of the all-tenants cost table + the per-tenant detail.

period_yyyymm is the calendar month the costs were aggregated over;
cost_pct_of_mrr drives alert_band. Per-intent-tier list is empty on
the all-tenants list endpoint (omitted server-side to keep the
payload light) and populated on the per-tenant detail endpoint.

cost_pct_of_mrr.description: variable total_cost_myr / tenant_mrr_myr, expressed as 0–N (not 0–1) — 0.5 = 50%. Above 1.0 means the tenant's variable cost alone exceeds what they pay.
cost_pct_of_mrr.title: Cost Pct Of Mrr

per_intent_tier.description: Empty on the all-tenants list endpoint (omitted server-side for payload size); populated on per-tenant detail.
per_intent_tier.title: Per Intent Tier

supabase_storage_cost_myr.description: Informational only — Supabase is now a FIXED platform cost (see PlatformCostSummary), NOT part of per-tenant variable cost. Retained for transparency / migration of the external Mimir gauge.
supabase_storage_cost_myr.title: Supabase Storage Cost Myr

tenant_name.description: Display name of the tenant for UI labelling.
tenant_name.title: Tenant Name

total_cost_myr.description: Per-tenant VARIABLE cost (Polaris COGS) = Anthropic in/out + Cohere + OpenRouter. EXCLUDES Supabase (now fixed). This is the marginal cost of serving the tenant.
total_cost_myr.title: Total Cost Myr

TenantCostMonthly.title: TenantCostMonthly

TenantInvoice.description:
Read shape for ``GET /api/admin/billing/invoices`` (and the
per-id endpoint).

Columns from the merged 008 + 054 schema. Legacy ``pdf_url`` is kept
so pre-Phase-9 rows continue to read; new code populates
``pdf_bucket`` + ``pdf_object_key`` and lets ``pdf_url`` stay NULL.

due_at.description: RFC3339 UTC. NULL on pre-Phase-9 rows; populated for all new issues.
due_at.title: Due At

marked_paid_by_admin_id.description: platform_admins.id who clicked Mark Paid. NULL on auto-reconciled or pre-Phase-9 rows.
marked_paid_by_admin_id.title: Marked Paid By Admin Id

pdf_bucket.description: Supabase Storage bucket name. Pairs with pdf_object_key. New rows use this; legacy rows keep pdf_url instead.
pdf_bucket.title: Pdf Bucket

proration_basis.description: JSONB snapshot of proration inputs per 00c §12.4.1. Nullable in legacy rows.
proration_basis.title: Proration Basis

updated_at.description: RFC3339 UTC. NULL on pre-Phase-9 rows.
updated_at.title: Updated At

TenantInvoice.title: TenantInvoice

TenantProduct.description: Row shape for `tenant_products` plus its ordered image gallery.
TenantProduct.title: TenantProduct

TenantProductUpsert.description:
Body shape for create + update.

``tenant_branch_id`` may be explicitly set to None to clear the branch
scope on update. ``is_active`` defaults to True so a freshly created
product is immediately eligible for the bot's lookup; pausing requires
an explicit toggle off. Images are managed via the dedicated
attach/detach/reorder endpoints (PR-2), not this body.
TenantProductUpsert.title: TenantProductUpsert

TenantPromotionUpsert.description:
Body shape for create + update. ``tenant_branch_id`` may be
explicitly set to None to clear the branch scope on update.

``is_active`` defaults to True so a tenant creating a new promo
sees it immediately on the bot's lookup; pausing requires an
explicit toggle off.
TenantPromotionUpsert.title: TenantPromotionUpsert

TenantTemplateDTO.description:
Outbound GET /api/tenant/templates row.

Includes every column the portal lifecycle UI needs:
submission timestamps, current status, the meta_template_id (so the
portal can deep-link into Meta's Business Manager for templates that
were rejected or paused), and the rejection_reason text Meta returned.
TenantTemplateDTO.title: TenantTemplateDTO

TenantTemplateSubmit.description:
Inbound POST /api/tenant/templates body.

``name`` matches Meta's accepted pattern (lowercase + underscores).
``language`` is a Meta locale code (en_US, ms_MY, zh_CN). We don't
enum-restrict it because Meta's allowed set evolves; bad locales
surface as 400s from Meta which we wrap into MetaTemplateError.
TenantTemplateSubmit.title: TenantTemplateSubmit

WebhookEventBreakdown.description:
Webhook ingest errors over the last 24 h, grouped from ``webhook_events``.

Surfaces the operational ingest problems the volume/freshness webhook tiles
don't break out: HMAC failures, tenant-not-found, ChannelNotEntitled,
suspended-tenant drops. An "error" is any status NOT in the benign set
(received/processed/replay_ignored/human_handling/demo_routed/
non_message_event/chatwoot_deferred). ``by_status`` and ``by_error_class`` are
two additive views of the same total (both sum to ``total_errors_24h``);
``by_error_class`` aggregates an error_class ACROSS statuses and groups NULL
under '(none)'. Lists are capped server-side (top-N status/error_class, most
recent N rows). ``error`` is set ONLY when the probe itself failed (DB
outage) — the tile must show a distinct state, since all-zero counts would
otherwise read as a healthy "no errors".
WebhookEventBreakdown.title: WebhookEventBreakdown

WebhookEventCount.description:
One (key, count) bucket in the webhook-error breakdown.

``key`` is a ``webhook_events.status`` value (e.g. hmac_fail) or an
``error_class`` (e.g. ChannelNotEntitled:whatsapp), depending on which list
it appears in.
WebhookEventCount.title: WebhookEventCount

WebhookEventError.description: One recent non-success ``webhook_events`` row for the at-a-glance list.
WebhookEventError.title: WebhookEventError

WebhookSurfaceHealth.description:
Webhook surface counters drawn from webhook_events.

Reused for both telegram and meta webhook surfaces.
events_1h, hmac_fail_1h, and tenant_not_found_1h are windowed to the
last 1 h to give a fast-moving operational signal.

events_1h.description: Total webhook events in last 1 h.
events_1h.title: Events 1H

hmac_fail_1h.description: HMAC validation failures in last 1 h.
hmac_fail_1h.title: Hmac Fail 1H

last_received_at.description: RFC3339 UTC of most recent webhook event.
last_received_at.title: Last Received At

tenant_not_found_1h.description: Events with no matching tenant in last 1 h.
tenant_not_found_1h.title: Tenant Not Found 1H

WebhookSurfaceHealth.title: WebhookSurfaceHealth
